To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
somatostatin inhibits both TRH and growth hormone-replacing hormone-induced GH secretion in young and mature chickens.

(1) somatostatin inhibits basal and TRH-induced GH secretion in young and in adult chickens and that the effect of somatostatins is more potent in adult birds; (2) somatostatine also inhibits GRF-induced GH secretion in both young and adult birds; (3) the GH responses to TRH are more sensitive to the inhibitory action of somatostain than are the GH responses to GRF in both young and in adult birds

somatostatin inhibits growth hormone release in response to growth hormone-releasing hormone and thyrotropn-releasing hormone, and that the inhibitory effect is more pronounced in adults than in young chickens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the hypothalamo-hypophyseal system in the regulation of growth hormone (GH) secretion in chickens.
the regulation of GH secretion in the domestic hen and the role of the hypothalamo-pituitary portal system in this regulation.
the role of the endocrine system in the control of the development and maintenance of sexual behavior in the domestic hen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SRIF14 exerts its inhibitory influence on TRH-induced GH release in adult chickens, but that the effect is less apparent in young chickens.
somatostatin is a physiological regulator of GH release in the domestic fowl.
somatostatin does not inhibit GH release in the adult bird, but does inhibit GH release in young chicks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GH secretory responses to GRF and TRH in young and adult birds are inhibited by SRIF.
in adult chickens, SRIF14 is a potent inhibitor of TRH-induced GH release.
the chicken GH secretory response is inhibited by SRIF at the hypothalamus and pituitary levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that

somatostatin is able to suppress the release of growth hormone in both young and adult birds, but that the effect of somatostatins on TRH-stimulating growth hormone release is more pronounced in the adult bird.
the effect of SRIF14 is dose-dependent and that the sensitivity of TRH-induced GH secretion to SRIF14 inhibition increases with age.
SRIF14 can inhibit both basal and stimulated GH secretion in young and mature chickens.
